items.title: Protests intensify in India over demands for election chief to quit
items.author: Saurabh Sharma
items.creator: Saurabh Sharma
items.summary: Thousands of youth protesters and opposition supporters rallied in Delhi and Mumbai on Sunday to demand the resignation of India's election commission chief over changes to voter rolls, as police detained some demonstrators for a third day.
items.body:
Thousands of youth protesters and opposition supporters rallied in Delhi and Mumbai on Sunday to demand the resignation of India's election commission chief over changes to voter rolls, as police detained some demonstrators for a third day.
Opposition leaders Raj Thackeray and Uddhav Thackeray led protests in Mumbai, calling for the revisions to be scrapped and for Election Commission Chief [USN:L4N45K0DB TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar"] to step down.
The protesters say the changes benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's governing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), a charge denied by the Election Commission and the BJP.
In the capital, New Delhi, protesters started gathering in the early evening and some were detained by police, according to a Reuters witness.
Some demonstrators breached police barricades and surrounded vehicles carrying detained demonstrators, climbing onto them and laying on the road to block their path, the witness added.
"Police dragged me by my hair," said Aahna Singh, an activist and political science student at Jawaharlal Nehru University who was protesting. "The police are resorting to brutality."
Delhi Police did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment.
Police in the capital have prevented protesters from [USN:L4N45P01A TEXT:"assembling"] over the last two days, detaining dozens of them and transporting them away by bus.
Some of the detainees were released later on Friday and Saturday, but police registered cases against some on charges of violating orders banning mass gatherings in the centre of the capital.
PROTESTERS SAY VOTER ROLL CHANGES EXCLUDE MILLIONS The protesters say the nationwide voter-roll revision exercise launched last year has disenfranchised millions of eligible voters by removing them from electoral rolls in a way that will benefit Modi's party.
"I just want to tell the ruling party this much... We are angry about how you are wielding that power. It's the people of this country who should decide who sits in power and who sits in opposition, not the Election Commission," the opposition leader Raj Thackeray said.
The Election Commission says the exercise is designed to remove duplicate, deceased, or ineligible entries and maintain electoral integrity. On Friday, it directed its officials to register eligible voters inadvertently omitted from electoral rolls.
Kumar has not publicly responded to the demands for his resignation or commented on the protests, which look set to continue over the next few days due to more planned rallies.
An alliance of India's opposition parties plans to launch protests to "[USN:L6N45M0NH TEXT:"save democracy"]" with a march to the Election Commission office on Tuesday. The Gen Z Cockroach Janta Party has announced plans for a major rally in Delhi on October 10.
The demonstrations represent the latest in a series of youth-led challenges to Modi's government — unprecedented in his 12 years in power.
In July, student protests forced the ouster of the federal education minister following a leak of question papers for a national medical college entrance examination, marking the worst political crisis of Modi's third term in office.
(This story has been corrected to change the day of the opposition march to Tuesday, not Monday, in the third bullet point and paragraph 14.)

SEPANG, Malaysia, Oct 4 : George Russell's Formula One title hopes took a crushing blow when his Mercedes ground to a halt with a power unit failure five laps from the finish, turning what looked like a certain podium into heartbreak at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday.
The British driver was running in a strong position to claim valuable championship points when the second safety car emerged for Alex Albon's Williams, which was stuck in the gravel.
But as the field prepared for a thrilling finale behind the safety car, Russell - who was third behind eventual race winner Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli - suddenly parked his car on the main straight and shook his head as he climbed out.
"You've almost got to laugh, it's beyond disappointment. It's just so many times this season it's happened. It's a real shame," Russell said.

"The podium looked very certain. Solid race, not amazing race, but solid race. But not the first time, so I'm pretty used to this feeling."
The retirement meant Russell's championship deficit grew from 66 points to 84 behind Antonelli.
"I don't need to say I think it's (championship hopes) gone or whatever, but of course it's exceptionally unlikely and that's just the reality," Russell added.
"I knew if I wanted to come back, I needed luck on my side... It's a real shame."
Mercedes boss Toto Wolff confirmed it was a power unit failure on Russell's car.
"I'm so massively annoyed. I'm not in a happy place," Wolff said.
"First of all we didn't have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend, so there's a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I'm sure we will."
With the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc finishing third and fourth, Mercedes' lead in the constructors' standings is now 151 points.
"We had such an advantage (with) two safety cars, you couldn't be more unlucky," Wolff added.
"And to make things worse, a PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George, which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points.
"So as much as I love to be here, when I look at the pure races, one of my worst experiences, to be honest."

SYDNEY, Oct 4 : Dual-code international winger Mark Nawaqanitawase scored two tries as the Sydney Roosters edged the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in the National Rugby League final on Sunday, securing the foundation club a 16th title.
Nawaqanitawase, who could represent Australia at both the league and union World Cups over the next 12 months, crossed either side of halftime to help crush Newcastle hopes of a massive upset in front of a crowd of 80,814 at Stadium Australia.
Newcastle were looking to take the title back to their industrial port city for the first time since 2001 and scored the first two tries of the contest through Francis Manuleleua and skipper Kalyn Ponga to take an early 12-0 lead.
Nawaqanitawase, playing the final game of his two-year stint at the Roosters before his return to rugby union, cut the deficit from a clever kick and chase five minutes before the break, however.

Newcastle defended several sets on their own line at the start of the second half but Roosters centre Billy Smith forced his way over in the 47th minute for a converted try that locked up the scores at 12-12.
Sam Walker put the Sydney side in front for the first time with a penalty seven minutes later, and Nawaqanitawase added his second try in the right corner before the hour mark to extend the lead to 18-12.
Experienced five-eighth Daly Cherry-Evans, playing his last NRL game before his switch to England's Super League, slotted a field goal to extend the advantage to seven points but the Knights found a second wind in the remaining 11 minutes.
Summoning the spirit of last week's sensational win over the Penrith Panthers with 12 men that got them to the final, they forced their way upfield and winger Greg Marzhew crossed for a converted try that made it a one-point game with four minutes on the clock.
The Roosters, one of the two clubs remaining from the first season of what became the NRL in 1908, held on, however, to secure their first title since 2019 and fourth under long-term coach Trent Robinson.
"Credit to the Knights, they fought for 80 minutes there," said Nawaqanitawase.
"This is going to last me a lifetime, it's sad to go but I love everyone here, I love all the boys, and let's celebrate this win, far out."

Source: Reuters

items.title: Votação chega ao fim em eleição polarizada entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
items.author: Eduardo Simões
items.creator: Eduardo Simões
items.summary: As quase 500 mil seções eleitorais espalhadas pelo Brasil começaram a ser fechadas às 17h deste domingo, dando início à expectativa para a divulgação do resultado em uma disputa pela Presidência da República acirrada e polarizada entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).
items.body:
As quase 500 mil seções eleitorais espalhadas pelo Brasil começaram a ser fechadas às 17h deste domingo, dando início à expectativa para a divulgação do resultado em uma disputa pela Presidência da República acirrada e polarizada entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).
Marcada por polêmicas envolvendo desde o Judiciário até a padroeira do Brasil, passando por denúncias generalizadas de corrupção e temores de interferência externa, a campanha eleitoral para presidente chegou ao primeiro turno com a disputa totalmente em aberto entre os dois principais candidatos.
Lula e Flávio votaram no começo da manhã e manifestaram confiança na vitória.
Ao votar em uma escola em São Bernardo do Campo (SP), Lula fez um apelo para que os eleitores com mais de 70 anos comparecessem às urnas e reafirmou que o que estava em jogo nas eleições era a escolha entre o "fortalecimento do regime democrático e a barbárie".
Flávio Bolsonaro votou em uma escola em Vila Isabel, no Rio de Janeiro, pouco após a abertura das urnas, e disse que esperava vencer já no primeiro turno. "As nossas pesquisas internas mostram que a gente ultrapassou no primeiro turno já faz algum tempo", declarou. "Espero que seja suficiente para dar vitória no primeiro turno."
As pesquisas de intenção de voto divulgadas no sábado, no entanto, apontam para uma nova rodada de votação, que aconteceria em 25 de outubro.
Para a eleição acabar neste domingo, é preciso que um dos candidatos conquiste mais de 50% dos votos válidos, quando são desconsiderados os votos brancos e nulos.
Levantamentos do Datafolha e da Quaest colocaram Lula e Flávio em empate técnico no primeiro turno nos votos válidos, com vantagem numérica do atual presidente de 3 pontos na primeira e de 1 ponto na segunda. Uma outra pesquisa, do MDA, colocou Lula com 47,8% dos votos válidos contra 42,1% de Flávio.
O presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), Kassio Nunes Marques, afirmou confiar em um processo tranquilo de votação: "Amanhecemos o dia hoje com a segurança de que as eleições vão transcorrer na maior normalidade", disse, ao votar em Brasília no início da manhã.
Os mais de 158,7 milhões de brasileiros aptos a votar puderam ir às seções eleitorais ao longo do dia -- as urnas abriram às 8h e fecharam às 17h pelo horário de Brasília -- após meses de embates muitas vezes em nível pessoal de cada lado, em que as propostas para governar o país pelos próximos quatro anos não foram protagonistas.
A campanha chegou ao fim sem que Lula e Flávio tenham se enfrentado diretamente. No debate da TV Bandeirantes, ambos decidiram não ir, deixando os púlpitos vazios com seus nomes para serem criticados por Augusto Cury (Avante), Renan Santos (Missão) e Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), que estavam presentes. Romeu Zema (Novo) completa a lista dos outros candidatos cujos partidos têm representação no Congresso, mas cujas intenções de voto jamais se aproximaram da dos dois líderes.
Já o debate da TV Globo, que tradicionalmente encerra as campanhas, acabou sendo [USN:L1N45N18V TEXT:"cancelado"] após uma série de decisões judiciais e da desistência de última hora de Flávio, filho mais velho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro -- que está atualmente em prisão domiciliar após ser condenado por tentativa de golpe de Estado. Lula havia dito dias antes que não compareceria.
Nunes Marques disse esperar que candidatos acionem a Justiça com questionamentos relacionados às eleições, mas frisou, em entrevista coletiva nesta tarde, que a votação está transcorrendo com normalidade e transparência. Segundo ele, as urnas estão funcionando normalmente e não houve necessidade de votação manual em nenhum ponto do país.
TEMOR DE INTERFERÊNCIA A eleição também ocorre em meio a renovados temores sobre uma possível interferência estrangeira na eleição presidencial brasileira. A Reuters [USN:L6N45M0VR TEXT:"revelou"] na última semana que autoridades francesas e alemãs ouviram de membros da Agência Brasileira de Inteligência (Abin) que já estariam acontecendo tentativas de interferência dos Estados Unidos e da Rússia no pleito.
O diretor-geral da Polícia Federal, Andrei Rodrigues, afirmou neste domingo que a corporação já abriu investigação para apurar suposto esquema de financiamento de uma agenda de extrema-direita no Brasil pelo governo norte-americano de Donald Trump que teria entre os objetivos interferir nas eleições brasileiras.
A investigação foi solicitada pela Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU) na quinta-feira e teve como base reportagem publicada no jornal inglês The Guardian, segundo a qual o Departamento de Estado norte-americano teria destinado US$1 milhão de um fundo ligado aos direitos humanos e à democracia para um programa chamado "Combate ao Lawfare e à Censura no Brasil".
Nunes Marques enfatizou, no entanto, que o TSE não identificou nenhum indicativo de interferência estrangeira nas eleições. “Equipes que monitoram riscos internacionais não apontam qualquer tipo de risco”, afirmou.
Na última quinta-feira, a embaixada dos EUA no Brasil [USN:L6N45O0XD TEXT:"anunciou"] a suspensão dos serviços consulares a partir da sexta-feira, alegando preocupações não especificadas de segurança. Além disso, a embaixada pediu aos seus funcionários que trabalhassem de casa na sexta após uma ameaça. A embaixadora da Austrália também anunciou o fechamento da representação diplomática do país em Brasília citando o alerta norte-americano.
A medida foi criticada pelo presidente do PT, Edinho Silva, que viu tentativa do governo do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, de influenciar a opinião pública brasileira. Neste domingo, no entanto, Nunes Marques ponderou que a iniciativa seria usual no caso de eleições acirradas, e citou que teria acontecido o fechamento de embaixadas também durante o último pleito na Colômbia.
A relação com os EUA e com Trump foi um dos principais marcadores da diferença entre Lula e Flávio. Enquanto o presidente alertou o homólogo norte-americano publicamente a não interferir no Brasil, o senador procurou mostrar proximidade com Trump, inclusive visitando-o na Casa Branca.
"É uma relação tensa porque o Brasil não quer se ver dentro da zona de influência dos EUA. Tradicionalmente a nossa diplomacia é independente. O Lula acredita que, pela boa relação com a China, especialmente a comercial, que manter essa independência é fundamental", disse Leonardo Barreto, cofundador da Think Policy.
"O Flávio tenta fazer dos EUA uma espécie de fiador das eleições. A família Bolsonaro acredita que as eleições não são feitas em condições de liberdade. Desconfiança em relação a urna, meios de comunicação, administração do Judiciário. Buscam no apoio dos americanos uma espécie de pressão para garantir o mínimo de neutralidade das autoridades brasileiras, percebem nos americanos uma espécie de seguro", acrescentou.
BETS, STF E PADROEIRA Em meio a denúncias de corrupção como as do Banco Master e o escândalo do INSS, que atingiram tanto Flávio quanto o filho mais velho de Lula, além de ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), a campanha também foi marcada pelo apelo do senador à imagem de seu pai, ao mesmo tempo em que buscava se mostrar mais moderado do que o ex-presidente, enquanto Lula seguiu batendo na tecla dos seus três mandatos na Presidência e lançando mão de medidas populares às vésperas do pleito.
Entre elas, o governo anunciou o reajuste de 15% nos benefícios do Bolsa Família, a edição de uma medida provisória para proibir casas de apostas online e o anúncio da intenção de distribuir gratuitamente pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) as chamadas canetas emagrecedoras, três medidas aprovadas pelo eleitorado, segundo as pesquisas de opinião.
Mas a polêmica que marcou a reta final da campanha ficou por conta de rumores de que Flávio retiraria de Nossa Senhora Aparecida o título de padroeira do Brasil, o que foi negado com veemência pelo senador. Flávio classificou os boatos de "fake news", enquanto Lula disse que, enquanto for presidente, ninguém irá "avacalhar" com Nossa Senhora.
Além do presidente, os eleitores também escolherão neste domingo os governadores dos 26 Estados e do Distrito Federal, além de 54 dos 81 senadores e dos 513 deputados e dos integrantes das Assembleias Legislativas de 26 Estados e da Câmara Distrital do Distrito Federal.
A eleição para o Senado estará sob o foco, em um momento de pressão sobre ministros do STF, que podem sofrer impeachment pelos integrantes da Casa, e em um momento em que estão [USN:L6N45N0ZL TEXT:"vagas"] funções em órgãos reguladores, como o Banco Central, cujos nomes precisam ser aprovados pelos senadores.

items.title: Brazil's Bolsonaro takes early lead as results trickle in for high-stakes election
items.author: Brendan O'Boyle, Luciana Magalhaes, Rodrigo Viga Gaier
items.creator: Brendan O'Boyle, Luciana Magalhaes, Rodrigo Viga Gaier
items.summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, is seeking a fourth term as president while Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the 45-year-old son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, hopes to return his father's right-wing movement to power.
items.body:
Senator Flavio Bolsonaro took an early lead as Brazil began reporting results on Sunday afternoon in the first round of a tight presidential election, following a campaign dominated by corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling.
The field of 13 candidates has been led by two clear frontrunners — leftist [USN:L6N459162 TEXT:"President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva"], 80, who is seeking a fourth term, and Flavio, the 45-year-old son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who hopes to return his father's right-wing movement to power.
With about 32% of votes reported, Flavio led Lula with 50.74% of the votes to the president's 41.14%.
Early results showed southern states that lean to Bolsonaro reporting faster, while votes from Lula's northeast stronghold are tallied slower.
If no candidate wins more than 50% of valid votes, the top two will face off on October 25. Surveys show Lula and Flavio polling roughly even in a likely runoff.
A victory for the senator would extend a wave of wins across Latin America by right-wing candidates aligned with US President Donald Trump, while Lula's reelection could create a headache for Washington, which has clashed with his government over trade and security.
Despite growing worries over Brazil's public finances and sluggish economic growth, the campaign offered [USN:L1N4580UE TEXT:"meager policy debate"], as both leading candidates skipped the major TV debates.
UNDECIDED VOTERS While polls right up until Saturday showed Lula would likely lead the first round but not avoid a runoff, Flavio told journalists in Rio de Janeiro he was confident he could win the presidency in the first round, citing voters' frustration with his chief opponent.
Flavio was counting on "a protest vote from people who would otherwise vote for another candidate but are opposed to Lula," he said. "I hope it’s enough to secure a victory in the first round."
Thaise Lima, a 41-year-old lawyer on her way to vote in Sao Paulo, said her main goal was to get Lula's Workers' Party out of office.
"I don't think Flavio is the best candidate, but I might decide to vote for him in the next few minutes," she said, adding that she wished psychiatrist and author Augusto Cury were a more viable candidate.
Fernando Tempel, 49, a management consultant, told Reuters he was voting for Flavio despite initially planning to vote for Romeu Zema, the former governor of Minas Gerais state.
OUTSIDE INTERFERENCE On the other hand, Lula's allies have warned that the Trump administration might refuse to recognize election results if he wins, pointing to an aborted effort to [USN:L6N43R03C TEXT:"send US officials to Brazil"].
"What is at stake is the future of Brazil," Lula said after voting in Sao Bernardo do Campo, in Sao Paulo state.
Trump has not formally endorsed a candidate, though he hosted Senator Flavio Bolsonaro at the White House and praised him publicly.
"I'm a little worried about everything that's been happening recently, including internationally. I feel this election has had a lot of outside influence, more than in previous elections," said Cristiano, 34, a doctor in Brasilia who voted for Lula and preferred to withhold his surname.
"We are confident in our President Lula, who will fight for national sovereignty," said Pedro Palacio, 45, who was voting in Brasilia alongside his wife, Andreia, and their two sons and two dogs, all of whom wore outfits supporting the president.
As of Sunday afternoon, the election was proceeding normally, Brazil's electoral court chief Kassio Nunes Marques said in a press conference.
“Teams monitoring international risks have not identified any risks whatsoever," he said.
Reuters reported on Wednesday that Brazilian intelligence officials briefed a French and German delegation on [USN:L1N45E08V TEXT:"alleged US and Russian interference"] before the election. The US has rejected claims of interference in Brazil's affairs.
ECONOMIC HEADWINDS Despite [USN:L1N44111S TEXT:"falling inequality"] and unemployment, Lula has struggled to win over voters grappling with high living costs, heavy household debt and the threat of street crime and more pervasive gang activity.
Flavio Bolsonaro has sought to capitalize on cost-of-living concerns, while Lula has moved to ban online gambling and, as the race tightened, expanded welfare and proposed fresh debt relief for families.
Rising spending and public debt above 82% of GDP have stoked fiscal concerns that Brazil's next president will need to address. The government lowered its [USN:L1N45E0QC TEXT:"economic growth forecasts"] for this year and next to 2.0% and 2.3% respectively.
"I voted for Brazil to start growing again," said Marciano de Souza e Silva, a 52-year-old public servant in Brasilia and former Lula voter who moved right, voting for Jair Bolsonaro in 2018 and 2022 and Flavio on Sunday.
"The best social program is one that encourages people to start businesses, to actually produce real wealth," he said.
SCANDAL-PLAGUED CAMPAIGNS Overshadowing the policy debate, a scandal surrounding the now-defunct Banco Master has engulfed much of Brazil's political class and renewed public anger over corruption.
Daniel Vorcaro, who ran the bank, was arrested earlier this year and accused of a multibillion-dollar fraud scheme. The investigation has probed the banker's ties to figures from Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to Flavio Bolsonaro, who is being investigated for money laundering tied to the case by the federal police.
The candidate has denied any wrongdoing, although he confirmed raising millions of dollars from Vorcaro to make a movie about his father.
The banker's connections to Moraes, widely perceived as a Lula ally, [USN:L6N44U1B6 TEXT:"plunged the court into crisis"] a month before the vote, creating fresh problems for the president. Moraes has said the case against him is politically motivated for his role in the [USN:L1N45711X TEXT:"conviction of the elder Bolsonaro"].
On Sunday, voters will also elect all 513 lower house members and two-thirds of the Senate, where some lawmakers have pushed to impeach Moraes.
Congress has gained greater influence in Brazilian politics since the impeachment of former President Dilma Rousseff, a Lula ally, in 2016, raising the stakes of those legislative races.

items.title: “It never occurred to me that he wouldn’t do it”: Aaron Sorkin on Jesse Eisenberg's refusal to work in ''The Social Reckoning'
items.summary: Actor-director Aaron Sorkin admitted that "it never occured" to him that the actor Jesse Eisenberg wouldn’t be on board for the movie 'The Social Reckoning', which is a sequel to 'The Social Network,' ...
items.body:
“It never occurred to me that he wouldn’t do it”: Aaron Sorkin on Jesse Eisenberg's refusal to work in ''The Social Reckoning' Actor-director Aaron Sorkin admitted that "it never occured" to him that the actor Jesse Eisenberg wouldn’t be on board for the movie 'The Social Reckoning', which is a sequel to 'The Social Network,' in which he portrayed the young tech billionaire, reported Variety. 
ANI | Updated: 04-10-2026 22:29 IST | Created: 04-10-2026 22:29 IST

Aaron Sorkin and Jesse Eisenberg (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Actor-director Aaron Sorkin admitted that "it never occured" to him that the actor Jesse Eisenberg wouldn’t be on board for the movie 'The Social Reckoning', which is a sequel to 'The Social Network,' in which he portrayed the young tech billionaire, reported Variety. Speaking with Entertainment Weekly, as quoted by Variety, Sorkin recounted that he was “just a couple of pages from being done with the script for the new film when he ran into Eisenberg at a party and said, ‘I’m gonna be sending you something in a couple of weeks.’”
The actor “smiled and nodded, and I sent it to him,” said Sorkin. “It never occurred to me that he wouldn’t wanna do it,” as quoted by Variety. Sorkin continued, explaining he tried to convince Eisenberg, but he didn’t budge.
“This is the only time I’ve written myself an outline. I don’t do it for the movies, but I did it for my conversations with Jesse. It was arguments for why he should do it. They included, ‘We already know you’re gonna be great because you were already once.’ You know, ‘Here are the great moments that you’re gonna get to play in the movie.’ And I laid it out for him.” And while Eisenberg didn’t sign on, he did tell Sorkin that their conversations made him “come closer to changing my mind than I thought you were going to,” which the director said 'pleased' him," added Sorkin as quoted by Variety. Not even a sizeable paycheck could sway Eisenberg, admitted Sorkin.
“I knew what the studio was offering him to do it, but money does not motivate Jesse. It’s infuriating. If anything, money is a disincentive for him. It’s admirable. He’s very concerned about raising his kids with too much money,” said Sorkin, as quoted by Variety. In the lead-up to the release of “The Social Reckoning,” which hits theatres on October 9, Eisenberg’s refusal to return as Zuckerberg has been a hot topic.
Earlier, while speaking with Variety, Jesse Eisenberg said, “I just told [Sorkin] I’m moving in different directions in my life, and you know, what he said sums it up nicely. I don’t want to be associated with that character, but all of my reasons for not wanting to do the movie have nothing to do with how wonderful the movie is, and will be, and I’m sure is already.” 'The Social Network,' which also starred Andrew Garfield and Justin Timberlake, was nominated for eight Oscars and won three, including best adapted screenplay for Sorkin, best film editing and best original score. Eisenberg earned an Oscar nomination for his portrayal of Zuckerberg.
'The Social Reckoning' stars Strong, Mikey Madison, Jeremy Allen White, Billy Magnussen, Bill Burr and more. (ANI)

items.title: Two dead in flooding in Spain's Catalonia region
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Two people have died and another was missing after heavy rains and flooding in Spain's Catalonia region, authorities said on Sunday.
items.body:
Two people have died and another was missing after heavy rains and flooding in Spain's Catalonia region, authorities said on Sunday.
Catalan leader Salvador Illa confirmed the death of a man after a wall collapsed in Tordera, a town to the north of Barcelona, in a message on his social media account on Sunday.
Another person died in Montornès del Vallès, firefighters said on Sunday, while emergency services were searching for a missing person in Pineda de Mar, a town 52 km (32 miles) to the north of Barcelona.
Catalan authorities issued a red alert warning and urged people to stay inside from 8 p.m. (1800 GMT) on Saturday until Sunday at 2 p.m. (1200 GMT) because a "mini-hurricane" could hit the northeastern region, with more heavy rain forecast.
Homes were flooded and cars left submerged in Bellvitge and Cornella near Barcelona after torrential rain on Saturday. Ducks swam in huge puddles that formed on motorways in Barcelona.
Sarai Sarroca, director of regional weather service Meteocat, said on Saturday that the core of an exceptional weather system was over the Mediterranean and a "mini-hurricane" could move over land in Catalonia.
Flights were cancelled or delayed at Barcelona airport, La Vanguardia newspaper reported on Saturday.
All local trains were disrupted by the deluge. Shops shut early, football matches were called off and a performance of Verdi's Aida at Barcelona's Liceu opera house was cancelled.

items.title: Éthiopie-La capitale du Tigré sous contrôle des forces gouvernementales
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Les forces gouvernementales éthiopiennes et les milices alliées ont repris le contrôle de la capitale du Tigré, ont-elles déclaré dimanche, infligeant ainsi un revers majeur à l'alliance d'opposition qui gouverne cette région du nord.
items.body:
Les forces gouvernementales éthiopiennes et les milices alliées ont repris le contrôle de la capitale du Tigré, ont-elles déclaré dimanche, infligeant ainsi un revers majeur à l'alliance d'opposition qui gouverne cette région du nord.
Les Forces de paix du Tigré, une milice pro-gouvernementale dit dans un message publié sur Facebook que ses combattants avaient pris le contrôle de Mekelle, la capitale du Tigré.
Une source proche de la milice avait auparavant dit à Reuters qu'elle était entrée dans le centre-ville samedi après-midi, suivie par l'armée éthiopienne.
Le Front populaire de libération du Tigré (TPLF), qui dirige l'alliance d'opposition, a dit de son côté dans un communiqué publié sur Facebook qu'il s'était retiré de Mekelle, et que le gouvernement régional serait "temporairement transféré hors de Mekelle et opérerait depuis un autre endroit".
Une source humanitaire et un habitant de Mekelle, sous couvert d'anonymat, ont confirmé que la ville était désormais aux mains des forces gouvernementales.
Le cabinet du Premier ministre Abiy Ahmed n'a pas répondu dans l'immédiat à une demande de commentaire.
La prise de Mekelle par les forces pro-gouvernementales constitue une importante perte pour l'alliance d'opposition dirigée par le TPLF, qui avait lancé une vaste [USN:L8N45F0T4 TEXT:"offensive"] le 23 septembre contre l'armée éthiopienne.
Les forces fédérales éthiopiennes et les combattants alliés ont lancé une contre-offensive rapide dans le Tigré, mais selon les analystes, ces combats — qui constituent la pire escalade depuis la guerre civile de 2020-2022 — risquent de dégénérer en un conflit régional plus vaste.
Le gouvernement fédéral d'Addis-Abeba a rompu ses relations diplomatiques avec l'Érythrée la semaine dernière, l'accusant de soutenir l'alliance rebelle aux côtés du Soudan et de l'Égypte. Les trois pays rejettent ces accusations.

items.title: Government forces seize capital of Ethiopia's Tigray region from rebels
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Pro-government forces have regained control of the capital of Tigray, they said on Sunday, dealing a major setback to the opposition alliance that rules the northern Ethiopian region.
items.body:
Pro-government forces have regained control of the capital of Tigray, they said on Sunday, dealing a major setback to the opposition alliance that rules the northern Ethiopian region.
The Tigray Peace Forces, a pro-government militia, said in a post on Facebook that its fighters controlled Mekelle. A source close to the militia had earlier told Reuters it entered the centre of the city on Saturday afternoon, followed by the Ethiopian military.
The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), which leads the opposition alliance, said in a statement it had retreated from the capital and that the regional government would be "temporarily moved out of Mekelle and operate from somewhere else".
A humanitarian source and a Mekelle resident, who asked not to be named, confirmed the city was in the hands of government forces and their allies.
LOSS OF MEKELLE A MAJOR BLOW FOR TPLF The taking of Mekelle by pro-government forces is a major loss for the opposition alliance led by the TPLF, which [USN:L6N45G0U0 TEXT:"launched a big offensive"] on September 23 against the Ethiopian military.
Ethiopian federal forces have made a quick counterattack into Tigray, but analysts say the fighting — the worst escalation since a 2020-2022 civil war — threatens to escalate into a wider regional conflict.
The federal government in Addis Ababa severed diplomatic ties with Eritrea last week, accusing it of supporting the rebel alliance alongside Sudan and Egypt.
Egypt's foreign minister denied backing the TPLF and its allies. "I have to be very clear, we are not party to the domestic crisis facing Ethiopia now. It has nothing to do with us," Badr Abdelatty told Reuters on Sunday. Eritrea and Sudan also deny helping the rebels.
Abdelatty was speaking ahead of a meeting between Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and his Eritrean and Somali counterparts in Egypt on Sunday. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, the head of Sudan’s army, was also due to attend the talks.
Egypt and Ethiopia, two of Africa’s most populous countries, have been at loggerheads for years over Ethiopia’s construction of a major dam on the Nile River, which Egypt views as a threat to its water security.
“It is an existential issue. It’s life or death for 110 million people,” Abdelatty said.

items.title: Saudi Arabia quietly shelving NEOM Stadium, one of 2034 World Cup venues
items.author: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni
items.creator: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni
items.summary: It was meant to be one of the most ambitious venues for the 2034 FIFA World Cup.
items.body:
Saudi Arabia is quietly shelving plans to build one of its most ambitious stadiums for the 2034 FIFA World Cup, two sources familiar with the matter said, after delays and downscaling of the futuristic development housing it.
The NEOM Stadium was billed as an elevated arena in a glitzy 100-mile (160-km) steel and glass structure known as The Line, in turn part of the broader development known as NEOM.
NEOM was introduced about a decade ago as a centrepiece of de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's Vision 2030, an ambitious plan to diversify the economy and cut reliance on oil.
Yasir Al-Rumayyan, governor of NEOM's owner the Public Investment Fund, confirmed in April that The Line was [USN:S8N40J01E TEXT:"no longer a priority"], and said it was not vital before 2030, the original delivery target for its first phase. He denied any projects had been cancelled.
However, according to two sources, plans to build the NEOM Stadium have now been shelved indefinitely.
NEOM and the Saudi government media office did not reply to requests for comment, while Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Sports redirected questions to the World Cup 2034 Hosting Higher Authority.
The Authority said "substantial delivery" of construction milestones for the event was already taking place, but did not address questions around the NEOM Stadium and costs. It shared images of some of the other stadiums under construction.
RIYADH DEVELOPING 15 VENUES FOR 2034 WORLD CUP The 2034 World Cup is seen as a marquee event for Saudi Arabia, which under the Vision 2030 programme has invested heavily in sports via wealth fund PIF. The tournament will be the first time a single nation hosts the expanded 48-team format.
Riyadh is working to build or renovate 15 venues across five cities, as well as dozens of training facilities.
MEED Projects, a Dubai-based construction industry market intelligence platform whose team of analysts tracks tenders and projects in the region, puts the total value of the projects at $22.7 billion in data shared with Reuters.
According to MEED, NEOM's stadium is expected to cost $2.5 billion. It lists the projected 46,000-seat stadium in its data as "on hold".
The stadium has no listed completion date, according to the data, which describes the remaining stadiums and facilities as in various stages of development, with completion expected between 2026 and 2033.
Saudi Arabia is under increasing pressure from the Iran war, which has led to heavy disruptions to energy shipments and damage to critical infrastructure, with the kingdom facing attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis.
Last week, the Ministry of Finance said it [USN:L1N45M0WE TEXT:"expected"] a fiscal deficit this year wider than previously projected and a real GDP contraction of 3.6% following a drop in oil activities.
PIVOT FROM GIGA-PROJECTS The geographic distribution of the stadiums adds to the challenge of delivering the projects, a third source said. That could further be compounded by some projects set to host stadiums being delayed or downsized, such as The Line or Riyadh's New Murabba development, the source added.
In January Reuters [USN:L1N3YR0WK TEXT:"reported"] that Saudi Arabia has suspended construction of The Mukaab, a colossal cube-shaped skyscraper at the centre of the New Murabba.
Reuters also reported last year that the PIF was pivoting from its focus on costly giga-projects to endeavours with more immediate financial returns, a strategy [USN:L1N40Y0DC TEXT:"later articulated"] by Saudi officials.
Still, other projects for the World Cup are progressing. The [USN:L6N43I0ZY TEXT:"Aramco Stadium"] in the eastern city of Al Khobar is set to be completed by the end of this year and host its first game in January, for which tickets are on sale.
Work on other planned stadiums is going ahead, a fourth source said.

items.title: Latvian PM on track to lead pro-Ukraine coalition after election win
items.author: Andrius Sytas
items.creator: Andrius Sytas
items.summary: Andris Kulbergs has promised to improve governance and reduce public spending.
items.body:
Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs was set to retain power and form a pro-Ukrainian coalition after his centrist United List secured the biggest [USN:L8N45O1BP TEXT:"parliamentary election"] victory since Latvia regained independence in 1991.
With 97% of ballots counted after Saturday's election in the NATO and European Union country bordering Russia, United List was on 35.3%, enough for 42 seats in the 100-seat parliament.
A businessman and amateur rally driver, Kulbergs, 47, came to power in May after the previous coalition crumbled over its handling of incidents in which stray [USN:L8N41K055 TEXT:"Ukrainian military drones"] flew undetected into Latvia.
Latvia's economy has underperformed its Baltic neighbours for more than a decade and Kulbergs has vowed to improve governance, cut red tape and reduce public spending, political scientist Roberts Kits said.
"Kulbergs played on being a get-things-done type of guy and has persuaded the voters that he can do things differently, bring some fresh energy," he said.
"This means the responsibility is huge. People expect him to deliver, but the question remains whether he has the team to do it."
United List appeared able to secure a parliamentary majority with either the nationalist National Alliance or the liberal Progressives, Kits said.
"(Kulbergs) is smart, let's hope that something will be better, that he will change what can be changed", Aina Sturmane, 78, a pensioner, told Reuters in Riga on Sunday.
No Latvian government has survived a full term, and Kulbergs will face an uphill battle holding together the United List, a loose alliance of small parties and independents, said political scientist Janis Ikstens.
PM PLEDGES TO MAINTAIN HARD LINE ON RUSSIA Kulbergs pledged continuing support to Ukraine and to keep a hard line towards Moscow.
"Any economic ties with Russia makes us weak. Yes, it can bring some extra money, but it's a weakness Russia might exploit," he told reporters at his party's headquarters on election night as supporters celebrated the scale of the win.
"It's remarkably good. I was not expecting such a result," Kulbergs said.
Voter turnout was 51.8%, down from 59.4% in 2022, underscoring disappointment with politicians in Latvia, Ikstens said.
United List was followed by the populist, MAGA-style Latvia First, which was on 13.1%. Latvia First had courted the country's substantial ethnic Russian minority in the run-up to the vote.
Third in the ranking was the pro-Russian Sovereign Power party, on 11.7%, followed by the National Alliance, which promotes a hardline approach to the Kremlin, at 8.9%.
Throughout his campaign, Kulbergs promised more anti-drone capability for Latvia and to maintain defence spending at 5% of gross domestic product, one of the highest levels in NATO.
His pro-Kremlin rivals said Latvia should stop any aid to Ukraine and instead focus on tackling cost-of-living issues, particularly among the country's Russian-speaking minority.
Although pro-Russian parties increased their representation, Kits said they remained sidelined and were unlikely to influence government policy.
Latvia's ethnic Russian minority is split between those who oppose Moscow's war in Ukraine and others who voice frustration with policies at home aimed at limiting their influence on public life, which many of them see as discriminatory.
Latvia, with a population of 1.9 million, is sandwiched between the Baltic Sea and Russia and Belarus to the east, with EU and NATO allies Estonia and Lithuania to the north and south.

items.title: Haunted by grief, Gaza's displaced still wait overseas for return
items.author: Nidal Al-Mughrabi
items.creator: Nidal Al-Mughrabi
items.summary: Omar al-Hassayna fled Gaza for Cairo after an Israeli airstrike wiped out much of his large family. Three years on, he remains there waiting for enough stability, security and reconstruction in his still devastated homeland to return.
items.body:
Omar al-Hassayna fled Gaza for Cairo after an Israeli airstrike wiped out much of his large family. Three years on, he remains there waiting for enough stability, security and reconstruction in his still devastated homeland to return.
Hassayna is one of more than 100,000 Gazans who left the enclave during the war that was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, and who remain stranded overseas, according to Palestinian Authority figures. They still mourn dead relatives and their [USN:L1N45F09E TEXT:"destroyed homes"] and neighbourhoods.
"I left Gaza and came to Egypt, the land of Kinana (referring to Egypt), but at the same time, this will not be forgotten, my dear brother, it will not be forgotten," he said.
"I am waiting for the opportunity, I am waiting for the moment when Gaza becomes stable so I can return to my country, and be a productive member of this country, and be a positive force for the country."
Nearly a year after a ceasefire in Gaza that was meant to start a process of reconstruction under a technocratic government along with a political process that would lead to an eventual full Israeli withdrawal, little has changed.
Israeli forces still hold more than 60% of the territory and conduct almost daily airstrikes, while Hamas controls most of the area where Palestinians live, mostly in temporary shelters with what aid agencies call inadequate aid supplies and no prospect of reconstruction soon.
Some 308 members of Hassayna's [USN:L8N4400Z0 TEXT:"extended family"] were killed when Israeli strikes destroyed a cluster of Gaza City apartment buildings where they had gathered for shelter on November 22, 2023, according to Palestinian authorities.
Among those killed were his wife, four of their adult sons and four small grandchildren including an infant only a few months old.
Hassayna's oldest son Mohammed is also in Cairo along with his own four children, as is the widow of one of his dead sons with her daughter. He has brothers in the Egyptian capital too.
One daughter was medically evacuated to Turkey with her husband and six children, and another daughter remains in Gaza with her five children although her husband was killed in the attack.
The Israeli military did not respond to a request for comment on the details of the November 22 strike. It said its attacks in Gaza are directed at military targets, while trying to reduce harm to civilians.
ABOUT 7,000 PALESTINIANS HAVE RETURNED TO GAZA In August, Hassayna watched on video from Cairo as relatives buried 112 family members, including his wife, sons and grandchildren, whose bodies had been recovered from the rubble, with dozens still missing.
Hassayna owned a business selling tools for firefighting and safety equipment in Gaza and some of his goods survived the war. He periodically sells some to fund his stay in Cairo, where he has remarried.
All those who left Gaza were vetted before their departure by both Israel and Egypt, but many have found it hard to return to the territory.
Although some Israeli politicians have urged a policy of encouraging all Gaza's population to leave and to prevent those who left from returning, about 7,000 have gone home. Hassayna believes Egypt will stop any widespread displacement of Palestinians from Gaza.
However, no widespread return of those who fled Gaza may be likely until the territory's prospects are clearer.
"If Gaza returns. If there is an international agreement (with) a comprehensive situation for the Palestinian people and construction begins, why would I delay?" he said.

items.title: Revolut's rise to become Europe's $115 billion big bank rival
items.author: Lawrence White, Elizabeth Howcroft
items.creator: Lawrence White, Elizabeth Howcroft
items.summary: Revolut has become Europe's most valuable startup and a challenge to centuries-old banking giants, though it faces hurdles.
items.body:
Revolut has risen to become Europe's most valuable startup and a challenge to centuries-old banking giants, having grown rapidly since it was launched just over a decade ago as a fintech promising cheaper forex fees.
Yet Revolut faces many hurdles itself, with the amount of revenue it extracts per customer a fraction of its established competitors and a small lending business by industry standards.
A spokesperson for Revolut said in an email that the London-based company has a "diversified business model", earning its revenue from various products and services rather than lending.
"That means our growth depends on building things customers value, rather than on interest rates," the spokesperson said.
Here's Revolut's rise, in five charts:
GOING FOR GLOBAL CEO Nik Storonsky has stressed he wants Revolut to be truly global, expanding into markets [USN:L4N44E0AO TEXT:"from Mexico to Australia"].
The company has announced several new licences in recent weeks, as it aims to become one of only a handful of banks with retail operations spanning so much of the globe.
Meanwhile, some traditional lenders seen as global, including HSBC (HSBA.L) , are reducing their retail footprint.
Valued at $115 billion privately, Revolut is now worth more than Britain's Barclays (BARC.L) and France's Societe Generale (SOGN.PA) as investors bet on its tech platform winning over more customers globally.
Revolut's 2025 pretax profit was £1.7 billion ($2.2 billion), a fraction of Barclays' £9 billion, but growing fast.
Paulo Macedo, CEO of Portugal's biggest bank, Caixa Geral de Depósitos, said in June that 2025 was the last year in which the 150-year-old bank would record higher profit than Revolut.
"When you go to Europe the bank CEOs there are talking about Revolut as their most important threat because of their aggressive marketing and growth," said Cihan Duran, director at S&P Global Ratings.
MARRED BY SETBACKS In the US, where Revolut has a provisional license, it will face tougher competition, investors said.
"The US could be potentially the biggest growth for Revolut. But at the same time, the US is the most competitive market," said Konstantin Sidorov, CEO of the London Technology Club, which invested in Revolut when it was valued at just $5.5 billion.
There have been setbacks, including a fine in Lithuania for failing to prevent money laundering. Revolut said an investigation had not identified any confirmed instances of money laundering, adding that it had signed a settlement with the central bank and taken steps to resolve shortcomings.
And in September, Revolut accidentally sent customer data to hackers posing as government investigators. The company said its systems and customer funds were unaffected and it had contacted the "limited number of impacted individuals" to give support.
In 2024 and 2025, Revolut was the most-complained-about bank in Britain in fraud cases whereby customers are tricked into sending cash to scammers, Ombudsman data compiled by consumer advocacy firm Which? showed.
Revolut has previously said in response it takes fraud very seriously and has robust customer protections in place.
CUSTOMERS HAVE SURGED A striking measure of its growth is customer numbers.
In Ireland, for example, Revolut said that 80% of the adult population has a Revolut account.
Revolut's website shows it has 80 million customers, against 84 million for JPMorgan (JPM.N) and 41 million for HSBC.
REVENUE-PER-CUSTOMER IS LOW Revolut makes far less from each of its customers than traditional banks, a Reuters analysis of its figures shows. Average deposit balances are also much lower.
Lower per-customer revenue is in part because Revolut lends much less than traditional banks, instead relying on fees such as card subscriptions.
With just £2.2 billion in loans at end-2025, Revolut's loan-to-deposit ratio of 6% compares with 55% for HSBC and 86% for Societe Generale.
Scaling its lending business will introduce risks including managing big and complex credit exposures, while entering fiercely competitive local mortgage markets will not be easy, analysts and investors said.
TOO FEW PRIMARY ACCOUNTS Revolut has attracted customers with its easy-to-use app but executives acknowledge too few use it as a primary bank account.
Revolut declined to comment in its latest results on how many customers did so in 2025, but said the figure was up 45% from a year ago.
This metric is a focus for Revolut's biggest backers.
Alex Immerman, an investor at Andreessen Horowitz, which is known as "a16z", told Reuters it was watching for primary-account adoption, as well as total customer balances.
($1 = 0.7573 pounds)

items.title: Trump forms "Super Intelligence Force" to cement US dominance in next-gen AI
items.summary: In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, "Following the Historic White House Accord on Super Intelligence, where the World's most important Technology Companies came together, and confirmed their ...
items.body:
Trump forms "Super Intelligence Force" to cement US dominance in next-gen AI In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, "Following the Historic White House Accord on Super Intelligence, where the World's most important Technology Companies came together, and confirmed their responsibilities to the American People, I am announcing the formation of the Super Intelligence Force (SIF)."
ANI | Updated: 04-10-2026 19:15 IST | Created: 04-10-2026 19:15 IST

US President Donald Trump (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump has announced the creation of a new federal task force called the Super Intelligence Force (SIF) to centralise executive branch policies and lead national efforts in advanced artificial intelligence. The announcement builds on the administration's executive order, which replaced the terms "Artificial Intelligence" and "AI" with "Super Intelligence" and "SI" across all executive branch operations.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, "Following the Historic White House Accord on Super Intelligence, where the World's most important Technology Companies came together, and confirmed their responsibilities to the American People, I am announcing the formation of the Super Intelligence Force (SIF)." The order, titled "Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence," established that the US government will no longer recognise or use Artificial Intelligence or AI as terminology in official settings to the maximum extent permitted by law.
Under the presidential mandate, Trump said that the SIF is designed to serve as the government's primary liaison across civil society, safety advocacy, and private industry. Trump outlined the wide scope of outreach to "ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence." "The Super Intelligence Force is tasked with coordinating the effort of the Federal Government to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence, which many say is bigger than the Industrial Revolution, and the Internet, and will protect the interests, and improve the lives, of all Americans," he wrote.
Trump specified that the Super Intelligence Force will coordinate government engagement with "Federal Government's engagement with Consumers, Public Interest Groups, Religious Organizations, Critical Infrastructure Providers, and Super Intelligence Companies." The Super Intelligence Force will be led by a four-member leadership team spanning national intelligence, defence, regulatory, and federal personnel operations. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Chief Technology Officer and Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering Emil Michael, and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor will direct the agency.
Trump stated that the leadership group will report directly to "the President of the United States (ME!), and the Chief of Staff, Susie Wiles". Under the executive order signed by Trump earlier this week, the administration temporarily applies the existing statutory definition of artificial intelligence under Title 15 of the United States Code to "Super Intelligence."
Additionally, the directive sets a 60-day deadline for the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology (APST) to submit proposed legislative language to Congress to establish an updated federal statutory definition of "Super Intelligence" and recommend conforming amendments to existing US laws. Earlier, President Trump hosted a high-level luncheon at the White House with top technology executives—including SpaceX and Tesla chief Elon Musk, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Google CEO Sundar Pichai, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, among others—where he framed the technological leap as an unprecedented era for humanity.
Emphasising the scale of the sector, Trump had stated: "It is the biggest thing there is — maybe the biggest thing there's ever been. It's much bigger than the Internet. This is unbelievable growth for our country — and we have all of them."Following the meeting, tech leaders and administration officials briefed reporters on a White House Accord focused on developing Super Intelligence safely. Commenting on the initiative, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said, "We want to give the American people and our customers confidence that the technology works in the way we intended."
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei underlined the need for collaborative execution, stating,  "We all need to work together to make sure that we can win and we can win safely. If we do this right, if we work with the President and everyone here, we can win safely." Highlighting the defence and intelligence dimensions of the discussions, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton noted: "The consensus today around that national security issue was being a leader in America in AI is the most important thing for national security." (ANI)

items.body:
Andrius Sytas　Terje Solsvik

[リガ ４日 ロイター] - ラトビアで３日に実施された総選挙は、親ウクライナ・中道のクルベルグス首相率いる「連合リスト」が予想を上回る大差で勝利した。開票速報で明らかになった。ロシアによる攻撃の可能性に対する警戒が高まる中、多くの有権者が緊張感を抱えながら投票に臨んだ。

開票率８８％の時点で、連合リストの得票率は３６．６％。ポピュリスト政党「ラトビア・ファースト」 が１３．４％で続いた。

バルト諸国はこの数カ月、ロシアがウクライナ支援の切り崩しと社会不安の醸成を狙って、欧州各地で破壊工作やサイバー攻撃などのハイブリッド攻撃を仕掛けていると警告してきた。ロシア側は、こうした非難には根拠がないと反発している。

クルベルグス氏は３日夕、リガにある党本部で、「驚くほどよい結果だ。ここまでとは予想していなかった」と述べ、首相続投に意欲を示した。

開票速報によれば、単独過半数には達していないため、組閣には連立が必要となる。同氏は、ラトビア・ファーストとの連立は望まないと述べた。

親ロシアの「主権」は出口調査で得票率１１．６％で３位、ロシアに対する強硬路線を掲げる右派政党「国民連合」が９．１％だった。

クルベルグス氏は選挙戦で、対ドローン能力の強化や国防費を国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比５％に維持すると約束した。この水準はＮＡＴＯ加盟国の中でも最も高い部類に入る。ラトビア・ファーストは、国内のロシア系住民の支持取り込みを図った。

親ロシア政党は、ウクライナへの支援を全てやめて、特にロシア語を話す少数派の生活費の問題にもっと力を入れるべきだと主張した。

items.title: Leftist and nationalists lead in election for Bosnia's tripartite presidency
items.author: Branko Filipovic, Fedja Grulovic
items.creator: Branko Filipovic, Fedja Grulovic
items.summary: Voters are casting ballots for the central tripartite presidency and national parliament.
items.body:
A Bosniak left-leaning moderate, a pro-Russian Serb nationalist and a Croatian nationalist are leading Sunday's election for Bosnia's inter-ethnic tripartite presidency, the election commission said, based on ballots from more than 90% of polling stations.
The results were largely in line with expectations and with projections by the Poliwave tracking platform, although voter turnout was low at a combined 42.2% in Bosnia's two entities, the Bosniak-Croat Federation and the Serb Republika Srpska. Voters also cast ballots for the national parliament, alongside regional races in the two entities.
Voter frustration has grown over an economic slowdown, the slow pace of EU entry talks and a lingering political crisis in which ethnically based dominant parties from the two entities have repeatedly stalled decisions by the weak central government that links them.
Denis Becirovic, a Bosniak of the Social Democratic Party (SDP-BiH) and part of the current tripartite presidency, garnered 26.66% of votes in the Bosniak-Croat Federation, ahead of the candidate for the centrist and traditionalist Bosniak Muslim Party of Democratic Action (SDA). The two had been considered close favourites in the election.
Also leading in the Bosniak-Croat Federation was newcomer Darijana Filipovic of the nationalist and pro-European Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ-BiH), with 14% of the vote.
In Republika Srpska, Zeljka Cvijanovic, an existing member of the tripartite presidency from the Serb and pro-Russian nationalist Alliance of Independent Social Democrats (SNSD), secured 55.34% of votes, the election commission said.
Voting continued in some polling stations after the 7 p.m. (1700 GMT) deadline due to delays related to a new electronic balloting system, Bosnia's Central Election Commission head Jovan Kalaba told reporters in Sarajevo.
The election commission redesigned ballots and introduced new biometric voter identification and electronic scanners, which it said were aimed at curbing voting fraud.
Speaking in Banja Luka, the largest Bosnian Serb city, Milorad Dodik, a separatist and pro-Russian leader of the SNSD who visited Moscow and met Russian President Vladimir Putin last week, said his party's candidate Savo Minic won the most votes for president of the Republika Srpska entity.
"We have won the member of the (Bosnian) Presidency, and the president of the Republika Srpska. An unexpectedly high result," Dodik said.
Since the Bosnian war ended in 1995 under the US-brokered Dayton peace accord, the country has been split along ethnic lines into two entities linked by the weak central government and tripartite presidency.
Bosnia, which has struggled to recover from the 1992-95 war, secured EU candidate status in December 2022 and approval to open accession negotiations in 2024. Actual talks have not started, however, because the domestic legislatures have yet to enact core requirements such as bolstering judicial oversight and passing anti-corruption laws.
Borjana Kristo, the deputy-head of the Croat HDZ-BiH, said that overall progress could be made through dialogue after the elections.
"Bosnia must make progress solely on the principle of consensus, dialogue, and mutual respect," she told party supporters, cautioning against rhetoric that would drag the country backwards.
Many voters in the country of 3.4 million people say they want to move beyond divisive rhetoric but its politics have become deadlocked.
The EU and Russia have been vying for influence over Bosnia, with the EU seeking to expand its membership across the Balkans while Russia wants to slow that process down and preserve its influence over the Republika Srpska.
The US has also sought to bolster its influence in Bosnia, pushing for a $1.5 billion [USN:L6N40Y0SF TEXT:"pipeline project"] to import US liquefied natural gas. The EU has said, however, that the selection of the company for the project lacked competitive transparency, while Washington and Brussels have also clashed over the role of the [USN:L6N41N07W TEXT:"High Representative"], the international peace overseer for the country.

items.title: Minutas de la Fed y del BCE mostrarán temores sobre la inflación mientras se desvanecen las expectativas de subida de tasas
items.author: Christopher Condon, Vince Golle, Craig Stirling
items.summary: Ambos bancos centrales publicarán en los próximos días las minutas de las reuniones del mes pasado, en las que subieron los tipos de referencia, ante preocupaciones sobre las crecientes presiones infl ...
items.body: Bloomberg — La urgencia que mostraban los responsables de la Reserva Federal y del Banco Central Europeo por dar continuidad a las subidas de los tipos de interés de septiembre en las reuniones de este mes se ha atenuado a raíz de los datos de empleo poco alentadores de EE. UU. y de la grave tensión en los mercados financieros franceses. Ambos bancos centrales publicarán en los próximos días las actas de las reuniones del mes pasado, en las que subieron los tipos de referencia, cediendo a las preocupaciones sobre las crecientes presiones inflacionistas. En EE.UU., el sólido crecimiento económico ha estado impulsando el mercado laboral, lo que ha permitido a la Fed centrarse en la inflación. Las actas de la reunión de septiembre de la Fed, que se publicarán el miércoles, podrían revelar que muchos responsables políticos estaban profundamente preocupados por las tendencias subyacentes de los precios y esperaban subir los tipos al menos una vez más antes de que finalice el año. Sin embargo, los nuevos datos de empleo publicados el viernes mostraron una creación de empleo inferior a lo esperado y un crecimiento salarial mediocre, lo que se suma a las pruebas de que el mercado laboral no está contribuyendo a las actuales tendencias inflacionistas. A principios de semana, las revisiones del Gobierno al indicador de precios preferido por la Fed mostraron que la inflación ha sido algo más moderada este año. Lo que opina Bloomberg Economics: “El listón para una subida de tipos en octubre se encuentra ahora muy alto. Aunque las actas recuerden a los mercados lo agresivos que se mostraron los responsables en septiembre, los datos posteriores han reforzado los argumentos a favor de la paciencia. La persistencia de la inflación en el sector de los servicios podría mantener abierta la opción de una subida en diciembre, pero es probable que la Fed necesite pruebas más claras de que las presiones sobre los precios han resurgido antes de volver a endurecer la política monetaria”. —Anna Wong, Andrew Sacher y Eliza Winger. Además, dos altos responsables de la política monetaria —el vicepresidente de la Fed, Philip Jefferson, y el presidente de la Fed de Nueva York, John Williams— enviaron señales inequívocas, con solo dos días de diferencia, de que consideraban que no había mucha urgencia para que la Fed tomara otra medida. Los inversores rebajaron en consecuencia sus expectativas de una subida. Los responsables de la política monetaria de EE.UU. se reunirán los días 27 y 28 de octubre, pocos días antes de unas reñidas elecciones de mitad de legislatura, lo que amenaza con empañar el resultado con la política partidista. El jueves, el BCE publicará el acta de su reunión del 9 y 10 de septiembre, y los inversores estarán atentos a cualquier indicio sobre el momento en que se producirá la próxima subida de tipos del BCE. En la zona del euro, las últimas cifras mostraron que la inflación se aceleró en septiembre por encima de lo previsto, debido en gran medida a los costes energéticos provocados por la guerra. A pesar de que las presiones sobre los precios siguen siendo elevadas, los inversores consideran que hay muy pocas posibilidades de que se produzca una subida de los tipos de interés en octubre. La tensión en el mercado de bonos se ha extendido a nivel mundial, y Francia se ha visto especialmente afectada, ya que la fragmentación de su Parlamento aviva las preocupaciones sobre el presupuesto y el déficit. Por otra parte, los datos sobre el desempleo y el comercio de Canadá pondrán de manifiesto las repercusiones de la guerra arancelaria del país con EE. UU. Los bancos centrales de aproximadamente una docena de países tienen previsto fijar sus tipos de interés, y se esperan subidas en la India, Kenia y Perú. Haga clic aquí para conocer lo ocurrido durante la semana pasada; a continuación, le ofrecemos nuestro resumen de lo que está por venir en la economía mundial. Una de las principales atención se centrará en la decisión del banco central de la India sobre los costes de financiación, que se dará a conocer el miércoles. Los economistas esperan que el Banco de la Reserva suba su tipo de recompra al 5,5 %, sumándose así a sus homólogos de Japón, Australia y EE. UU. en la política de endurecimiento monetario. El banco australiano Westpac publicará el lunes los datos sobre la confianza de los consumidores, que probablemente mostrarán un nuevo descenso debido a la subida de tipos de la semana pasada. Japón publicará el martes los datos salariales de agosto, y la atención se centrará especialmente en si el aumento de los salarios reales se ha mantenido por octavo mes consecutivo. Taiwán, Tailandia y Filipinas publicarán las cifras de precios al consumo a lo largo de la semana, y se prevé que los tres países muestren una aceleración de la inflación en septiembre. A lo largo de la semana, varios países publicarán datos sobre sus reservas de divisas; en este sentido, habrá que prestar especial atención a Corea del Sur, Taiwán y China para comprobar si parte de los fondos procedentes de sus crecientes superávits comerciales se refleja en las cifras. India y Tailandia también lo harán. Hacia finales de la semana, o posiblemente a principios de la próxima, el banco central de China anunciará los datos de crédito correspondientes a septiembre, que se seguirán de cerca para comprobar si se produce un cambio de tendencia respecto a la caída de la concesión de créditos observada en agosto. Es probable que los problemas fiscales de Francia sigan ocupando un lugar central, lo que centrará la atención en el BCE como posible salvador. Entre las intervenciones previstas de los responsables de la política monetaria figuran las del economista jefe del BCE, Philip Lane; el austriaco Martin Kocher; y el belga Pierre Wunsch. El acta de la reunión de septiembre del banco central, que se publicará el jueves, también será objeto de un minucioso análisis. Se intensifican las maniobras de cara a la selección de los nuevos responsables del BCE. Tanto el director del Banco de Pagos Internacionales, Pablo Hernández de Cos, como el exgobernador del banco central neerlandés, Klaas Knot —candidatos rivales para suceder a la presidenta Christine Lagarde— participarán en el mismo acto el lunes. El canciller alemán, Friedrich Merz, tiene previsto reunirse con ambos candidatos, incluido Knot, en los próximos días, según fuentes familiarizadas con el asunto. Los ministros de Finanzas de la zona del euro podrían iniciar las deliberaciones sobre el sucesor de la miembro del Comité Ejecutivo Isabel Schnabel cuando se reúnan en Luxemburgo el jueves. Esa reunión también será objeto de un estrecho seguimiento debido a la agitación en el mercado de bonos francés. Entre los datos más destacados de la zona del euro figuran varias publicaciones del sector manufacturero. A partir del martes, Alemania publicará, en días consecutivos, los datos sobre pedidos industriales, producción industrial y exportaciones. A lo largo de la semana también se darán a conocer las cifras de producción de Francia, España e Italia. Los retos industriales de la región acapararán la atención cuando el comisario de Comercio de la Unión Europea, Maros Sefcovic, visite Pekín a finales de esta semana. Las declaraciones del Banco de Inglaterra podrían resultar clave en el Reino Unido, que se enfrenta a sus propios retos en el mercado de bonos. Está prevista la intervención de cinco responsables, entre ellos el gobernador Andrew Bailey el jueves. La inflación sueca se publicará el jueves, tras el giro del Riksbank hacia una probable subida de tipos. En Noruega, donde el banco central subió los tipos el mes pasado, el índice de precios se dará a conocer el viernes. En Sudáfrica, el gobernador del Banco de la Reserva, Lesetja Kganyago, intervendrá el martes con motivo de la publicación del Informe de Política Monetaria. Hay varias decisiones monetarias previstas: El Banco Central de Colombia publicará el lunes el acta de su decisión sorpresa del 30 de septiembre de subir el tipo de interés de referencia en un cuarto de punto, hasta el 12,25 %. La decisión dividida de la junta refleja que las condiciones monetarias restrictivas están empezando a moderar, aunque aún no a revertir, el repunte de los precios al consumo de 2026. Los datos de inflación de septiembre podrían dar la razón a la decisión del Banco de la República. El consenso preliminar apunta a que la inflación general volverá a subir desde el 6,24%, más del doble del objetivo del banco central. México también publicará las actas de la reunión de septiembre de su banco central y los nuevos datos sobre los precios al consumo. Banxico, aunque mantuvo la tasa en el 6,5 % por tercera reunión consecutiva, pasó a adoptar una orientación basada en los datos. Al igual que en Colombia, es probable que los datos de septiembre muestren que la inflación se ha acelerado una vez más. En el ámbito de la política monetaria, los bancos centrales de Perú y Uruguay se enfrentan a decisiones difíciles en las reuniones de la próxima semana. En Perú, la inflación de septiembre se situó aún más por encima del objetivo, lo que podría hacer que el gobernador Julio Velarde y sus colegas perdieran la paciencia tras un año con el tipo de interés en el 4,25%. El banco central de Uruguay ha mantenido su tipo de interés de referencia en el 5,75% desde el recorte de 75 puntos básicos de marzo, y podría verse acorralado, por un lado, por la contracción de la economía en el segundo trimestre y, por otro, por cinco meses de datos que muestran un crecimiento más rápido de los precios al consumo. Los datos de inflación cierran la semana, y se espera que Chile y Brasil registren cifras más elevadas para septiembre —por encima del 4,1% en el primer caso y del 4,22% en el segundo—, en ambos casos por encima del objetivo. Las elecciones de Brasil del domingo, en las que se enfrentan el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, de 80 años, y su rival de derecha Flávio Bolsonaro en una contienda demasiado reñida como para pronosticar un ganador, podrían agitar la situación en la mayor economía de América Latina. El Banco Central de Venezuela publicará las cifras de inflación mensual y anual; la autoridad monetaria del país reanudó la publicación de estas cifras a principios de 2026. Los incrementos mensuales se moderaron por debajo del 10 % en agosto, frente al 32,6% registrado en enero, lo que moderó la tasa anual hasta el 534,2%. --Con la colaboración de James Mayger, Laura Osman, Monique Vanek, Robert Jameson, Piotr Skolimowski y Mark Evans. items.title: Merz unveils fresh military aid in Kyiv, says Germany won't be intimidated
items.author: Andreas Rinke, Felix Hoske
items.creator: Andreas Rinke, Felix Hoske
items.summary: Germany's chancellor said Moscow was trying to break the morale of the Ukrainian people, and announced €350 million for repairs in the energy sector.
items.body:
Germany will not be intimidated into dropping its support for Ukraine, Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Sunday as he announced a further €1 billion ($1.1 billion) in military aid during a visit to Kyiv marked by Russian drone attacks.
Air-raid sirens and explosions rang out repeatedly across the Ukrainian capital as Merz and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy visited a memorial to soldiers killed during the four-year-old war, as well as the [USN:L1N45K0A2 TEXT:"Academy of Sciences"], where at least two people died in a drone strike last week.
Russia has escalated its drone attacks on Kyiv and other cities in recent weeks, targeting telecoms, electricity and transport infrastructure as well as military assets.
Speaking at a press conference alongside Zelenskiy, Merz said Moscow was trying to break the morale of the Ukrainian people, and announced €350 million for repairs in the energy sector. He said Germany remained Ukraine's strongest backer.
DEALS WITH GERMAN COMPANIES WORTH €6.6 BILLION "We do this not only to protect Ukraine's territorial integrity; we do it deeply in our own interest, for it is a matter of Europe's security," Merz said, noting that Russia was carrying out cyberattacks and disinformation campaigns that struck at Europe's democratic order.
"This demonstrates that we will not be intimidated," he said.
Russia has said accusations of hybrid warfare are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria.
German officials said executives from companies, who travelled with Merz, had signed 14 agreements with the Ukrainian government and businesses worth roughly €6.6 billion.
Among those deals, Ukraine inked an agreement with Germany's Diehl Defence for the supply of IRIS-T air defence missiles, as well as a deal for radar equipment with Hensoldt and for jet drone interceptors with Quantum Systems.
"What is important in this visit is that not only Germany is helping Ukraine, but Ukraine is sharing its knowledge, experience, as well as orders," Zelenskiy said. "These are jobs for Germany."
Zelenskiy praised a new jet drone interceptor, dubbed SPYS and developed by Quantum, for showing promising results. He said Ukraine and Germany were close to [USN:L1N44U0N8 TEXT:"finalising a broad defence deal"], which he has previously said would include the production of drones, missiles and related software.
ZELENSKIY VOWS TO RESPOND Since the summer, Russia has targeted civilian and military infrastructure daily with dozens of high-speed jet-powered [USN:L8N4521KI TEXT:"attack drones"] – which Ukraine has struggled to down because they are much faster than previous propeller versions.
One of the Russian strikes on Sunday hit the Northern Bridge across the Dnipro River, damaging its roadway, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Telegram. The explosion injured two people and damaged a hot water supply system in the area, he said.
Zelenskiy said Russia's decision to escalate air strikes against infrastructure targets was due to setbacks it had suffered on the battlefield, and he vowed that Ukraine would retaliate. He said Russian President Vladimir Putin wanted to force residents to flee Ukraine's major cities.
"If our bridges collapse, we will manage to get out of this situation, but his people will feel it too ... This is maximum escalation of this war," Zelenskiy told reporters.
Russia has been [USN:L1N45P00Z TEXT:"attacking"] Kyiv's bridges since last week in an effort to disrupt links between the capital's two sides and logistics routes between central and eastern Ukraine.
MERZ APPEALS FOR END TO 'SENSELESS WAR' Zelenskiy said US peace envoy Steve Witkoff has messaged him to urge a return to trilateral talks as soon as possible. He said Ukraine was willing to meet this month and hoped Russia would join, but he said Western allies needed to apply more pressure to Moscow to bring the war to an end.
Earlier in the day, during the visit to the badly damaged Academy of Sciences, Merz appealed to Putin to "put an end to this senseless war".
"We are ready for talks, we are ready to discuss bringing this war to an end, but these barbaric attacks on the civilian population of Ukraine must stop," the German leader said.
Russia's Foreign Ministry [USN:L1N45P03K TEXT:"said"] on Saturday that Moscow would continue to systematically hit targets in Ukraine in what it said were retaliatory strikes for Ukrainian attacks on Russia. It warned foreign nationals and diplomatic staff against travelling to Ukraine.
($1 = 0.8887 euros)

items.title: テニス＝世界ランク1位シナー、マスターズ上海大会欠場を発表
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - 男子テニスの世界ランキング１位、ヤニク・シナー（２５、イタリア）は３日、長引いている膝のけがの影響で、マスターズ上海大会（７日開幕）を欠場すると発表した。

シナーは７月１２日にウィンブルドン選手権決勝でアレクサンダー・ズベレフ（ドイツ）を下して以来、公式戦でプレーしていない。２０２４年のマスターズ上海大会では、決勝でノバク・ジョコビッチ（セルビア）を下し、優勝した。

シナーはインスタグラムのストーリーズに「残念ながら今年はマスターズ上海大会でプレーできない。上海のファンの前でプレーするのは楽しいだけに、来週プレーできないことを申し訳なく思う」とつづり、「来年会えることを楽しみにしています」と締めくくった。

シナーの今年の成績は４４勝３敗。ウィンブルドンで四大大会５回目の優勝を達成した。

今年のマスターズ上海大会にはディフェンディングチャンピオンのバレンティン・バチェロット（モナコ）、同大会４回優勝のジョコビッチ、世界ランク２位のズベレフ、同３位のカルロス・アルカラス（スペイン）らが出場する。

items.title: ゴルフ＝ロッテ選手権で山下が6位浮上、ティティクル単独首位
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - 米女子ゴルフのロッテ選手権は３日、米ハワイ州エワビーチのホアカレイＣＣ（パー７２）で第３ラウンドを行い、山下美夢有が６位に順位を上げた。

７位でスタートした山下は６バーディー、１ダブルボギー、１ボギーの３アンダー６９でラウンド。通算１２アンダーの２０４とした。同じく７位で出た畑岡奈紗は２アンダー７０で回ったが、通算１１アンダーの９位に後退した。

岩井千怜と笹生優花はともに４アンダーで回り、通算９アンダーの１８位に浮上した。吉田優利と竹田麗央は通算８アンダーの２４位。西郷真央は通算７アンダーの３０位。西村優菜は４２位、櫻井心那は５３位、岩井明愛は６５位となった。

通算１７アンダーに伸ばしたジーノ・ティティクル（タイ）が単独首位。ユン・イナ（韓国）とポリー・マック（ドイツ）が３打差の２位で並んでいる。

items.title: テニス＝ルバキナ、世界ランク1位としての初戦で逆転負け
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - テニスの中国オープン（ＯＰ）は３日、北京で試合を行い、女子シングルス２回戦で世界ランキング１位のエレーナ・ルバキナ（カザフスタン）が初戦敗退を喫した。

この日が初戦となった第１シードのルバキナは、アリーナ・チャラエワ（アルメニア）と対戦し、第１セットは６─３で奪ったものの、続くセットを４─６、３─６で落として逆転負け。９月の全米ＯＰで優勝し、キャリア初の世界ランク１位となったルバキナだが、トップに浮上した後の最初の試合で敗れた選手としては、大坂なおみに次ぐ史上２人目となった。

ＷＴＡランキングは１９７５年に初めて発表されたが、ＯｐｔａＡｃｅによると、それ以降で世界ランク１位の相手に逆転勝ちを収めた選手では、今回のチャラエワ（１１８位）が最もランクの低いプレーヤーだという。

ルバキナは「間違いなく、今日は非常に厳しい試合だった。全米ＯＰで優勝してからいろいろなことがあった。睡眠や回復の機会をあまり持てなかった。アリーナをお祝いしたい。彼女は素晴らしい試合をした」と話した。

items.title: ＮＢＡ＝ピストンズ、デューレンとの契約延長を正式に発表
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）のピストンズが３日、制限付きフリーエージェント（ＦＡ）のセンター、ジェイレン・デューレン（２２）との契約延長を正式に発表した。

これまで米スポーツ専門チャンネルＥＳＰＮとジ・アスレチックは５年総額２億ドル（約３１６億円）と報じていたが、チームは契約の詳細を明かしていない。

ピストンズのバスケットボール運営部門代表を務めるトラジャン・ラングドン氏は「今後何年もジェイレンをチームの中心に据えられることをうれしく思う」とし、「彼は若くして多くを成し遂げており、われわれは彼の全盛期はこれからだと信じている」と述べた。

報道によると、ピストンズは最近デューレンに同じ総額２億ドルの契約を提示したものの、体重に関する条項を盛り込んでいたという。今回の合意では同条項が削除されたと報じられている。

昨季初めてオールスターとオールＮＢＡに選出されたデューレンは、レギュラーシーズンで自己最多の１試合平均１９．５得点に加え、１０．５リバウンドを記録。ピストンズは６０勝２２敗で東カンファレンス最高成績を残した。一方、プレーオフでは同１０．２得点、８．５リバウンドに数字を落とし、チームは東カンファレンス準決勝でキャバリアーズに３勝４敗で敗れた。
